# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other kids his age, which has been observed during playtime and physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Mealtimes can be a challenge for him. He has trouble eating certain foods and digesting them properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: He was slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: He's had a glue ear before, and the doctors have checked it out and provided treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, which has been noticeable for a while now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: His teeth have weak enamel, and the parents take good care of them through regular brushing and dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: He moves a bit differently compared to his peers, and his coordination and balance seem less developed than what you'd expect for a child of his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review to assess for heart conditions
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise, especially if sacral dimple is present

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks to have things repeated because he didn't quite catch what was said, suggesting hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes often, especially when trying to focus, suggesting vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to express himself clearly, leading to frustration when he can't get his point across.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel health.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone age and potential skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioural challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had feeding difficulties since she was little, with aversions to certain foods and textures, making mealtime challenging. Introducing new foods gradually and finding alternatives is part of her management.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated easily in crowded or noisy places. Preparing her in advance for such situations and finding quieter spots helps.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss. Many children require multiple grommet insertions, and some need hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness), which is a challenge, especially in school. Exploring options for glasses or contacts to correct it is ongoing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require a lot of care due to a propensity for cavities and tooth decay, necessitating frequent dentist visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly transferring to special schooling or remaining in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with communication, leading to frustration, and is attending speech therapy to improve her communication skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones leading to increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage tooth decay and cavities.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems such as hypermetropia.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart valve issues.
* Neurological management and medication adjustment as needed to control seizures.
* Speech therapy to improve communication skills.
* Consideration of a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy as necessary to support development and manage behavioural differences.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than other kids her age, even after short periods of play, which may be related to a heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, including an aversion to certain foods, making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences seizures, which can be scary and require management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing concerns, as she doesn't always respond when called, which may indicate a hearing problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, where her eyes turn inward sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful brushing and a restricted diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and is not talking as much as other children her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed fontanelle closure issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curved 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent chips or breaks
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight review to assess and manage vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and manage symptoms
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Management and treatment of epilepsy and seizures
* Support and management of feeding difficulties and dietary restrictions

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and requires additional support.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily and can't keep up with his friends during physical play, which may be related to a heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is a slow gainer and has less weight gain compared to his peers, requiring close monitoring of eating habits to ensure nutritious meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, with stiffer muscles than usual at times, and is working with physiotherapists to improve mobility.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear in the past, which was treated with antibiotics, and there are concerns about potential long-term effects on hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away, often squints, and may have myopia, with further tests pending to confirm.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger-than-usual front teeth, which are being monitored to prevent orthodontic issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testes, which require follow-up appointments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and prevent orthodontic issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to confirm myopia and potentially correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess potential heart conditions.
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess potential skeletal anomalies.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and mobility issues.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with eating and feeding, which is being addressed with therapists.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing soft sounds and turns the TV volume up really high to hear it properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means he's extremely far-sighted and has difficulty seeing things up close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, which makes his teeth more prone to cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky about food and refuses to eat certain things, making it a challenge to ensure a balanced meal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was developmentally slower to sit, stand, or walk, and currently has some differences in movement compared to peers, including stumbling more easily and trouble with balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe. Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing some sounds and often asks for the TV volume to be turned up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away, squints, and leans forward to get a better look.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important. Regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues may affect her learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many attend mainstream primary school with additional support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally slower and has some differences in movement and balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stumbles more easily and has trouble with balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to address conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to correct vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality with her heart that requires regular monitoring to ensure the condition does not worsen over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, including discomfort and pain, which are managed through dietary adjustments but not completely resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed with medication and monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, although in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves multiple times before she understands what was said, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions and some needing hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or books, suggesting difficulty seeing things clearly unless they are right in front of her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, particularly when consuming cold foods, which started recently and seems to bother her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, with careful brushing being very important, and regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable speech delay and does not speak as much as expected for her age, which are concerns for her parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or remaining in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially given the patient's difficulty with understanding speech without repetition.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems and potential need for corrective measures.
* Continued monitoring of the patient's heart condition to ensure it does not worsen over time.
* Management of seizures through medication and monitoring.
* Speech therapy to address speech delay and encourage increased communication.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's development and manage any behavioural differences.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which has been an ongoing issue despite dietary adjustments and encouragement to drink plenty of water.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has less coordination than her peers, struggles with tasks like tying shoelaces or riding a bicycle, and has challenges with gross motor skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have difficulties with neurological development.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty concentrating in environments with background noise, often asks to have things repeated, and speaks louder than necessary, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision, which can be concerning, and has been noted to squint during reading.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods and drinks, which causes her discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and regular dental check-ups are important.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's difficulty in articulating her thoughts and needs clearly affects her ability to express herself effectively and can lead to misunderstandings.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's challenges with coordination and gross motor skills, as well as her difficulty with articulating her thoughts, impact her development and behavior.

* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and correct any vision problems.

* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed with diet and occasional medication under the doctor's guidance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily when running around or playing actively and has speech delay, for which she is working with a speech therapist.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear once, which took a while to clear up, and her hearing is monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means her eyeballs are slightly larger than usual, and this has been noticeable since birth.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is working with a speech therapist to address her speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and tires easily, which may be related to developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and many have developmental delay.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing is not affected by the previous ear fluid issue.
* Ophthalmology review to monitor the patient's hypermetropia and prevent any further vision problems.
* Speech therapy to address the patient's speech delay.
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioral therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioral concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty swallowing certain textures and refuses many foods due to how they feel in her mouth, making feeding a challenge since infancy. Despite this, she has managed to maintain a healthy weight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. Lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was diagnosed with hypotonia, which means her muscles are weaker than they should be, affecting her overall strength and ability to participate in certain activities without getting overly fatigued. Physical therapy has been helping to some extent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has instances where she doesn't respond to her name being called, suggesting potential hearing issues. This happens in both quiet and noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on something, whether close up or far away, and gets headaches after reading or watching TV for extended periods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth that are protruded, which might affect her self-esteem or make eating certain foods difficult.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen and requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues might affect her schoolwork or everyday activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Monitoring of the patient's hip dysplasia and adherence to the recommended exercises and check-ups with orthopedic specialists.
* Consider referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any other skeletal anomalies.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble with feeding as a baby, including latching on and spitting up, but this has improved over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired after playing outside or running around and has difficulty keeping up with her friends, suggesting possible issues with energy levels or endurance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media when she was younger and has had trouble with her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia and has trouble seeing things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences sensitivity in her teeth, especially with cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems developmentally behind her peers and has trouble with speech, including jumbled words.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many require special educational support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and speech difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and speech difficulties
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular check-ups with the cardiologist to monitor the heart condition
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal anomalies

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups, indicating a need for ongoing monitoring of heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties with eating and digesting certain foods, making mealtimes a struggle.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which is a challenge to manage and understand how to best support him through episodes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have hearing difficulties, as he responds to some sounds but not others clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth, which is a noticeable concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind other children in development, indicating potential learning difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans at the secondary level.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delay and potential learning difficulties may contribute to behavioral challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers, which may be related to an underlying condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, spinal issues, and hip dysplasia, which can impact mobility and daily functioning.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to assess and address any hearing difficulties.
* Eyesight review to evaluate and correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor heart health and address any concerns.
* Consideration of a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and address challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been having a hard time gaining weight like other kids her age.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects her muscle tone.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes has to ask for things to be repeated because she didn't quite catch everything the first time, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and needs glasses.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip really easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and are prone to dental concerns, including large front teeth and other dental anomalies.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers than usual.

* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal health.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more easily than other kids his age, even after short periods of play, which may be related to a heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient does not gain weight as quickly as other kids and has atypical feeding patterns and digestion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has tethered cord, which may cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media (ear infections) and has trouble with his ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and trouble seeing things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, myopia, and hypermetropia.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs frequent dental visits due to prone teeth and constant monitoring for cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and prevent cavities
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems
* Check position of testes in boys to address undescended testes
* Consider a palate review to address feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for a cardiac review to address potential heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to address potential skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences exhaustion easily, even during simple playtime, and has been noted to have a heart condition that requires monitoring to prevent overexertion.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movement challenges, including accidents that affect her self-esteem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number require longer-term tube feeding, but specific gastrointestinal issues are not commonly highlighted in the syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach developmental milestones such as walking and sitting, and there are concerns about her overall developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, and includes delays in rolling, sitting, walking, and playing with toys, with a wide range of eventual abilities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and turns the TV up loud, indicating a potential hearing problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and is waiting to see if glasses will help.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, myopia, hypermetropia, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, necessitating regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues may affect her learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans due to the challenges of mainstream secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with communication and expressing her needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may benefit from medication or behavioural therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with her fontanelle not closing properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth size and enamel strength.
* Regular hearing reviews to address conductive hearing loss and potential need for hearing aids.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems such as myopia.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition and prevent overexertion.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and communication challenges.
